age.evidence: Age of mice not stated in the manuscript.

sex.evidence: Sex of mice not stated in the HTR methods.

psychedelic: 5-methylpsilocybin (with DMT and psilocybin as positive controls referenced from prior work)

dosing.doses_raw: dose-dependent increase; ED50 of 1.23 (95% CI 0.76-1.98) mg/kg
dosing.evidence: Mice (n = 5/group) were injected intraperitoneally (IP, 5 mL/kg) with drug or vehicle (saline)... Intraperitoneal administration of 1 produced a dose-dependent increase in head-twitch counts (F(4,20) = 9.61, p = 0.0002), with an ED50 of 1.23 (95% CI 0.76-1.98) mg/kg.

assays.assay_description: Mice injected i.p. with 5-methylpsilocybin or vehicle, then head movement recorded in a glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil for 30 min; head twitches detected via ResNet-50 + SVM classifier.

application_type.evidence: Mice (n = 5/group) were injected intraperitoneally (IP, 5 mL/kg) with drug or vehicle (saline)

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test habituation to the cylinder is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: head movement was recorded in a glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil

food_restriction.evidence: Test conducted in a glass cylinder with no food present during the 30 min recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Test conducted in a glass cylinder with no water present during the 30 min recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were injected intraperitoneally... and then head movement was recorded in a glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil for 30 min.

outcomes.summary: 5-methylpsilocybin produced a dose-dependent increase in head-twitch counts over a 30-min session (ED50 = 1.23 mg/kg, ~4.11 µmol/kg), making it more potent than DMT but less potent than psilocybin (historical positive controls).
outcomes.evidence: Intraperitoneal administration of 1 produced a dose-dependent increase in head-twitch counts (F(4,20) = 9.61, p = 0.0002), with an ED50 of 1.23 (95% CI 0.76-1.98) mg/kg.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total HTR counts were analyzed using a one-way ANOVA.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data are the mean ± standard error of the mean of HTR counts over the entire test session.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of transitions or behavioural sequences.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is a stereotyped drug-evoked motor response, not a natural ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Mice tested individually in a glass cylinder.

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR does not require learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: deep features are extracted using the pretrained convolutional neural network ResNet-50, and then the images were classified using a Support Vector Machine algorithm.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Total HTR counts were analyzed using a one-way ANOVA.

E1_environment_type.evidence: head movement was recorded in a glass cylinder

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in the recording arena.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects in the cylinder.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water available in the cylinder.

D1_continuity.evidence: head movement was recorded... for 30 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: HTR behavior was assessed continuously for 30 min.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same single behavioural assay (HTR) with consistent scoring; consolidated as one entry.
Set food_restriction and water_restriction to 'during' (standard short test apparatus with no food/water in cylinder), agreeing with qwen/glm over gptoss's 'not_reported'.
time_to_assay set to acute_0to2h / 0 min since recording began immediately after injection (per methods), per qwen/glm; overrode gptoss's 'not_reported'.

Dosing entries for DMT and psilocybin from gptoss were dropped because the paper only references their ED50 values from prior work using identical methods; they were not administered in this study's experiments.
n_total set to 25 (5 groups × 5/group, consistent with F(4,20)).
